exwayboard.com.title: Exway Atlass Pro
exwayboard.com.text:
Honestly really disappointed with my recent experience with the Exway Atlas Pro ecosystem.

Before buying the Atlas Pro, I specifically chose Exway because I wanted a premium and highly customizable board that I could gradually upgrade into a serious off-road monster setup.

Unfortunately my experience has been the opposite.

First, my charger failed/burned after only the second charging session.

Then I upgraded to 175mm off-road tires and ordered the official AP-5H16W66T pulleys because:

- Exway references 175mm + 66T setups on their website,
- dealers sell 175mm kits with 66T pulleys,
- and multiple community posts mention 66T for 175mm tires.

However, the pulley physically does not fit my hubs.

Initially support told me I basically needed to push/install it harder, but later another support representative admitted that my Atlas Pro hub revision only supports 56T pulleys and is incompatible with 66T.

Apparently there are multiple undocumented hardware revisions and compatibility differences depending on the hub generation.

Now I am stuck running 175mm tires on 56T pulleys, which causes:

- weaker acceleration,
- weaker braking,
- lower efficiency,
- more drivetrain stress,
- and worse battery consumption.

I understand mistakes happen, but this has been extremely frustrating for such an expensive “premium” ecosystem.

The most disappointing part is the inconsistent compatibility information between:

- the website,
- dealers,
- community guidance,
- and Exway support itself.

At this point I’m honestly considering selling the board and moving to another brand because I originally bought into Exway for the promised upgrade ecosystem and customization potential.

Just wanted to share my experience in case someone else runs into the same Atlas Pro / 175mm / 66T compatibility situation.

When a Premium Board Becomes a Repair Obligation

I went into my experience with Exway expecting a reliable, premium electric skateboard. What I received instead was a product that required constant intervention—and a company that avoided resolving the issue directly.

From the very beginning, the board had problems. I requested a refund early on, while the situation was still simple and fixable. Instead of honoring that request, Exway chose to repeatedly send replacement parts and instructions, effectively turning a brand-new purchase into a do-it-yourself repair project.

On paper, that might look like support. In practice, it felt like deflection.

Each issue was met with another shipment, another attempted fix, and another expectation that I would troubleshoot the product myself. At no point did this feel like ownership of the problem on their end. It felt like a slow process of wearing the customer down until they accept the situation.

The most concerning failure was structural.

The battery enclosure—arguably one of the most critical components of an electric skateboard—is made from cheap plastic that does not inspire confidence. In my case, that concern became reality. The battery component physically detached from the board. That is not a minor defect. That is a safety issue.

This wasn’t just about inconvenience anymore. It was about trust in the product itself.

What makes this experience even more frustrating is that it aligns with broader concerns surrounding the company. Exway has previously faced backlash over battery-related issues, including shipping boards with altered battery specifications without clearly informing customers in advance  ￼. Reviews across platforms also show recurring complaints about battery failures and lack of effective support when things go wrong  ￼.

In other words, this doesn’t feel like an isolated incident.

I documented everything—video evidence of the failures, the condition of the board, and the results of the attempted fixes. This is not speculation or exaggeration. It is recorded, repeatable, and real.

At its core, the issue is simple:

When a product fails early, the responsibility should not shift onto the customer to repair it piece by piece.

A straightforward refund request at the beginning would have resolved everything cleanly. Instead, the situation was extended through temporary fixes that never addressed the root problem.

Exway presents itself as a high-performance brand. My experience suggests something else: inconsistent quality, questionable material decisions, and a customer service approach that prioritizes avoiding refunds over delivering real solutions.

If you are considering buying from Exway, understand this:

You may not just be buying a board. You may be accepting responsibility for maintaining and repairing it from the moment it arrives.

And if something goes wrong, resolution may not come easily.

If you are considering Exway, understand this:

You may be stepping into a process—one where ownership quietly becomes obligation.

backfireboardsusa.com.text:
Who is this review for? Anyone considering purchasing from them who might be new to the world of electric skateboards and particularly those that might be considering purchasing from abroad (outside of the USA).

Why is this important? If you are buying a replacement component, you may get caught in an extremely frustrating and expensive Tech Support & Sales loop. You might think tech support and sales as a loop might not be in the best interest of the consumer and you would be right but it works really well for Backfire.

How does that work? They won’t disclose clear and complete upgrade paths for replacing components on your existing hardware and you have to contact Tech Support and then they have you. Welcome to the Tech Support & Sales loop.

Why is this bad? For each of the following steps in the loop you may have to incur the following: cost of part + international shipping (could be 78%+ of cost of part)  + import duty and taxes (which can be considerably inflated due to high shipping costs) for example for a new 9 pin hub motor this cost me $189.00 + $5.75 (insurance) + $95.46 (shipping) = $290.21 (total). As a nice surprise £41 import duty & taxes charge.

What is the Tech Support & Sales loop?

You buy a replacement part for your board and discover that the part is for a new version of your board so you contact support. 
They propose that you solve the issue by purchasing another new component. (you pay cost + shipping + duty)
The part arrives, you discover that there are no instructions and there is another incompatible set of parts, you contact support.
They propose that you solve the issue by purchasing another new component. (you might pay cost + shipping + duty)
You discover that there are no instructions for the two new components that are designed to work together and they are unsafe to ride as is, you contact support.
They propose that you solve the issue by purchasing another new component specifically designed to make the two new components that were designed for each other safe to use together. (you might pay cost + shipping + duty)

What did I do? I tried to dispute these shipping costs as all of these could have been minimized into a single shipment had my request for support had been responded to with a complete upgrade path outlining everything that needed to be purchased and how it can be assembled and used together. Failing to do this should have as a show of good faith resulted in comping the cost of the remainder of the upgrade which they failed to disclose when asked directly.

backfireboardsusa.com.title: Where do I start?
backfireboardsusa.com.text:
I decided to go with BackfireUSA for my deck as Iam building a DIY e-board. I've heard many positive things about the company. I saw online they have a used deck selection for $59.99 over the new for $79.99. Boy did I mess up over $20. The deck arrived without a box or packaging. It was just cardboard folded over and cheaply wrapped in plastic wrap. I did not feel good about opening it. 

Upon opening, I immediately notice how bad of shape it's actually in.
Not only is the deck expired, the layers of wood are actually separating and someone tried to glue or epoxy the separations all the way around the edge. I immediately sent an email to BackfireUSA. Now I did receive a quick reply by a guy named Jerry. After sending him the photos of the damage, his response was "It was probably from the previous owner before they turned it in." He was courteous and gave me a refund for the deck. He told me they are out of the new decks for $79.99. I thought that was it. So I figured I would at least try and fix the deck. After 45 min of sanding off the glue, I then notice that the wood is not only separating but it is also completely warped and uneven. 

I mean I understand things happen, but this is just unacceptable and should not of been sent out. How the person packing my order did not notice the glue all the way around the edge is a mystery. Just an overall bummer of a deal. Here I thought I would get a nice used deck to start my first build off, instead I receive someones totaled deck. 

Now this is my experience and obviously not everyone's but still, the company and it's employees should be held accountable and to a higher standard. I would of been happy to send back the deck and pay a little more money for a NEW current G2 or Zealot deck etc. Instead I was just issued a $59.99 refund and told they are out of those decks for a few weeks...

I was really excited to get into e-boarding and make this into a new hobby. Instead the company has left me with a horrible feeling and questioning is this actually for me...

I then turned the board off, put it all back in its original box and contacted Evolve customer support. They informed me NOT to use the board further as the board is now a hazard due to the smoke and fire risk and that I should immediatly send it in to the service center to be looked at. 

After a a few days long lengthy battle with the customer service reps trying to charge me about $80 to send it in, I was finally able to send the board off to the service center via FedEx.

After a few days I received an email from the service centre informing me that the board had indeed failed and the ECU was fried. In that same email Evolve tried to blame the problem on user error, stating that I was not running the correct air pressure in my tyres, causing too much strain on the ECU. This was nothing but pure speculation and accusation seeing as board didn't even have tyres on it when it was received at the service center, nor did those tyres have any air in them because I let them down to take off the tyres when the board had its fault. Your rep informed me not to use or touch the board any further as it was a hazard so I packed it up as it was at the time of that phone call. I have always used the air pressure recommended by the Evolve service rep on the companies YouTube channel. My board has always been extremely well maintained and treated with respect. For me personally, $2099 is a lot of money to spend on a product; so I have treated it like gold. 

They have on multiple occasions told me that my board is NOT covered by Australian Consumer Warranty; which in of itself is fraudulent. They have denied my right to a refund on approximately 5 different occasions.

I have compiled a file FILLED with stories, photos and videos of people having the EXACT same issue and also people having extremely similar issues with their Evolve GTR Skateboards. These boards are nothing but a safety hazard and must be avoided at all costs. 

This has been an almost 5 month saga and this entire time I've been without my board as it's still in Evolve's possession. It's my only form of transport because I'm disabled and can't drive. 

I'm currently working with a legal team to take them to court to get my money. With the help of my lawyer, I have sent off a final refund request this afternoon giving them 14 days to comply otherwise with the help of my lawyer we will be taking further legal action.

The have no respect for their customers or the law. Zero.

They could not care less about you and your expierience with their products, they just want your money. 

Also don't believe the reviews on their websites an/or their social media forums. They quickly delete any critical reviews that are made and even went to the extent of banning me from posting on their Facebook forum for a month all because I mentioned this issue there. evolveskateboardsuk.co.uk.title: Board Lost, Threats Made, Delays, and No Resolution After Months
evolveskateboardsuk.co.uk.text:
I feel it’s important to share my experience with Evolve UK so other customers know what they may be dealing with.

I originally sent my Evolve Hadean in for repair. Evolve kept my board for months with very few updates. On 8 July, I received an email saying that if I did not pay the repair invoice within 30 days, my board would either be returned unrepaired at my cost or disposed of. Under that pressure, I paid the £567.40 invoice.

After paying, I then found out the battery they invoiced me for wasn’t even in stock. I was left waiting for over a month for the part to arrive, with no proactive communication, I had to keep chasing myself.

When the repair was finally completed, Evolve arranged return delivery through their chosen courier. On 17 September it was marked as “delivered”, but nothing was delivered. I reported this the same day.

After weeks of back-and-forth, I was told the courier could not provide GPS evidence and the board had been lost in transit. Evolve then admitted that their claim to DHL was denied because they had not been submitted the claim within DHL’s 21-day window — a delay caused by their handling.

More than seven weeks have passed. I’ve been left without my board, without the £567.40 service I paid for, and without any fair offer to compensate me for the loss of a working Hadean with a brand-new battery.

What concerned me most is that, when I tried to resolve this, Evolve UK quoted the Consumer Protection from Unfair Trading Regulations 2008 against me - a law designed to protect consumers from traders. Using that legislation in this context felt inappropriate and intimidating for a customer simply asking to be compensated for a board lost in their care.

I’ve now had to issue a formal Letter Before Action, as I’ve exhausted every attempt to resolve this reasonably.

I’ve been an Evolve fan for years, but this has been the worst customer service experience I’ve ever had. I sincerely hope the parent company addresses how the UK distributor handles repairs and customer issues, because this has been unacceptable from start to finish.

either go with another brand or just throw 400 quid out the car window now, save your teeth and dignity.

www.kugooescooters.com.title: WARNING
www.kugooescooters.com.text: WARNING to Swedish buyers. This is a Chinese company that ships the goods from a Polish warehouse to customers in Europe. You can choose Swedish as the language on their website and pay with Klarna (which makes you feel safe as a consumer) but in fact they are violating the Swedish Consumer Purchase Act and EU directives because according to KuKirin's terms and conditions of purchase, customers do not have the right to a 14-day right of withdrawal. They sold a KuKurin G3 to my 15-year-old son but they write on their website that they do not sell to individuals under the age of 18. They also do not inform about the Swedish legal requirements on their website (that the electric scooter is considered a moped according to Swedish law). This in turn means that according to Swedish law the driver must have a moped driving license, register the electric scooter as a moped with the Swedish Transport Agency and pay motor insurance. In addition, it may not be driven on sidewalks and a fifteen-year-old must wear a helmet. If the police stop a teenager for illegal driving, the parents must pay a fine and may risk losing their driving license. KuKirin's Chinese customer service did not want to cancel the purchase when I pointed out that they had sold it to my 15-year-old son who, according to Swedish law, is not allowed to drive it because he does not have a driver's license. We had to sell it to a private individual (an adult with a driver's license) but we sold it at a loss. It was an expensive experience for us to buy from them. There are many private individuals in Sweden who sell KuKirin on the marketplace Blocket after only having test driven it, probably for the same reason as us (that they did not know that electric scooters are considered mopeds in Sweden).

kugoo.eu.title: Cold after-sales treatment
kugoo.eu.text:
I’ve been using my scooter for some time now, and while the scooter itself has been genuinely useful in my daily life, my experience with the brand has been far from ideal.

First of all, I bought the scooter and one year later the Kukurin update came out. Honestly, that’s something that could’ve been implemented much earlier, but fine — upgrades happen.

What really disappointed me were the brake pads. They wear out extremely fast. I have to replace them every 4 months, which becomes a constant and unnecessary expense. And speaking of expenses, the prices of the accessories on the official website are simply unrealistic. Considering I spent around €1000 on the scooter, I genuinely expected at least the first replacements to be included or offered at a fair price. Apparently, that’s not the case.

When I asked the team whether alternative pads from other stores would fit — since I found cheaper and more accessible options — I barely received any response. It felt like the only interest was pushing me to buy directly from their website at those same inflated prices.

Then the charger stopped working. And even though it was only slightly past the 1-year warranty, the response I got was basically:
“The product is out of warranty, the product is out of warranty.”
Written twice, in a way that honestly felt unusually harsh and cold.
I’m not used to this kind of treatment — especially after spending a small fortune. I don’t think anyone deserves to be spoken to like that.

To make it worse, the first reply they sent me actually said they could replace it if I paid €15 for shipping. But later they completely changed the stance and said that wasn’t possible after all — leaving me with no option other than paying €60 for a new charger on the website.

And I want to be very clear: I genuinely believe the people working at the front office are good people. I don’t think the problem lies with them individually.
But in any business, the most important part of the whole process will always be the customers. And the tone, communication style, lack of flexibility, and overall approach simply didn’t reflect that.

In conclusion, while I do appreciate the scooter itself and how useful it has been, the after-sales support, communication tone, accessory pricing, and warranty handling have left me genuinely disappointed. For a product at this price point, I expected much more care, professionalism, and understanding.
